decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach: left toward white car, right toward wooden pig. Gradually turn grippers downward; object heights estimated from RGB.
Replan from executed first step with smaller forward and rotation increments to respect joint continuity.
Continue downward orientation while aligning above the nearer white car and the wooden pig, keeping height before final descent.
Use slower increments after continuity interruption; align open grippers above target objects without descending to contact yet.
Slow both rotation and translation further so tracking can settle. Continue top-down alignment toward white car and pig.
Pause between small downward rotations to reduce accumulated tracking error; check gripper geometry and target alignment before grasp descent.
Correct for wrist-to-finger offset: shift back from baskets and laterally toward white car/pig while completing a slow downward wrist turn.
RGB shows watch at left jaws and pig at right jaws, rather than car. Center the watch, close both, and lift to visually test retention before sorting.
Both objects appear retained after lift. Raise clear of basket rims, transporting left watch toward middle blue basket and right pig toward right red basket.
Watch slipped and is visible on table; do not count it sorted. Keep pig closed, advance slightly into red basket while lowering; return left toward watch for retry.
Release pig into red basket and retreat right for the other wooden toy. Align left open jaws over the dropped black watch for a deeper centered grasp.
Lower left jaws around watch strap, close fully and test a small lift. Right approaches remaining wooden toy; pig is visible inside red basket.
Left watch now spans both jaws; lift and start toward blue basket. Center right jaws leftward around wooden toy, close fully, and test lift.
Carry retained watch over middle basket. Right toy appears to have slipped backward; reopen and shift back/down for a centered second grasp.
Set watch into blue basket and open left gripper. Lower right more deeply around wooden toy, close, and lift gently to verify retention.
Watch released inside blue basket. Lift retained wooden toy and start transport toward red; left withdraws toward the remaining silver watch.
Silver watch is centered in left wrist view: descend, close, then test lift. Keep wooden toy closed and carry toward right basket above rim height.
Both grasps visually retained. Advance wooden toy fully over red basket, release and retreat. Lift silver watch clear and carry toward middle blue basket.
Release second watch farther inside blue basket. Both wooden toys are visible in red. Start right-arm reset by withdrawing while gradually restoring upright wrist; left turns toward cars.
Approach white car with left arm, rolling jaws toward the car's narrow dimension while maintaining the approach axis. Continue right reset within its own workspace.
Fine-align left over white car and finish jaw roll, then close around the body. Bring empty right arm near its original pose with small continuous increments.
Lift white car vertically to confirm retention, then begin transport toward left white basket. Hold empty right arm at its original open-gripper pose.
White car slipped onto table. Reopen and use a more vertical approach with jaws across its current narrow dimension; align above the shifted car before retrying.
Car is aligned in yaw but forward of the jaw contact region. Shift diagonally and descend with open jaws, then inspect before closure.
White car now centered lengthwise between jaws. Descend slightly to engage sidewalls, close fully, and lift vertically to check retention.
White car remains between jaws after the test lift. Raise above basket rim and transport toward left basket, keeping orientation and grip unchanged.
Car has rotated within the grasp but remains retained. Advance slowly over left basket before release, maintaining closed jaws and right-arm home hold.
White car fell outside basket; reopen and retreat from reach limit. Reorient toward its new pose for a deeper sidewall grasp rather than counting a placement.
Previous retreat was rejected before execution. Replan with much smaller initial withdrawal increments from the observed near-limit configuration.
Move open left jaws above the side-lying white car and rotate to its long axis. Descend more deeply than the earlier shallow grasps; keep right at home.
Observed descent tracking error suggests rim interference. Move away from basket edge while centering the car and rotating jaws to its current axis; keep open for alignment.
Basket rim still obstructs descent. Withdraw left wrist backward with jaws open, then lower only after clearing rim to reach the side-lying car.
Rim is clear and tracking restored. Center around car midsection with a small yaw adjustment, descend to engage its sidewalls, and close before a minimal test lift.
Correct malformed no-motion right-arm row; reissue from unchanged observation. Lift the centered car grasp vertically, then begin the left-basket transfer.
Car slipped again and is now upside down. Use a vertical, lower sidewall grasp aligned to its present axis rather than the earlier shallow roof contact.
Center the upside-down car belly between pads, lower another small amount for full side engagement, close and perform a slow 16 mm test lift.
Keep the deeper belly grasp fully closed and lift vertically without lateral acceleration, checking that car rises before attempting another basket transfer.
Car remains securely between pads after vertical lift. Transfer slowly toward left basket with a modest forward tilt to keep the wrist away from the reach limit.
White car is still retained over its assigned basket. Move slightly farther inside, lower modestly, release, and withdraw without disturbing the basket.
White car is released in left basket. Approach the remaining yellow car with open jaws and align across its width; keep right arm reset.
Yellow car is right and below wrist center. Back away from the basket rim while descending to center open jaws around its sidewalls.
Continued rim interference and right-offset car require more backward clearance. Withdraw in small steps before resuming descent with open jaws.
Yellow car is centered and rim clearance restored. Lower to engage its sidewalls, then close fully and settle before lifting.
Test yellow-car retention with a slow vertical lift and uninterrupted fully closed command, keeping right arm at home.
Yellow car was not retained. Reopen and switch to a vertical approach, compensating wrist-to-pad offset while aligning above the car for a deeper retry.
Vertical approach is clear. Correct the car's left offset in wrist view, descend to the lower sidewalls, and close while stationary.
Car moved during closure and sits too far below the jaw region. Reopen, lift slightly, recenter along its length, and close again around the midsection.
Test the recentered yellow-car grasp with a gradual straight lift, holding jaws fully closed and avoiding lateral motion until retention is visible.
Yellow car is retained though rotated. Add rim clearance, then carry toward left basket with a gentle forward tilt, maintaining closed jaws.
Yellow car slipped during transport and is on the table. Return open jaws above its new position with a vertical approach for a deeper, centered side grasp.
Descend vertically with open jaws, making small longitudinal and lateral corrections to center the yellow car before closing lower around its body.
At grasp depth, yellow car is below and left of the jaw region. Recenter without further descent, then close on its midbody rather than bumper.
Yellow car is now centered squarely between both pads. Lift slowly and vertically, keeping orientation fixed and jaws closed to verify a stable body grasp.
Car remains retained after rotating in the grasp. Add clearance and advance slowly toward the left basket, using only a small gradual forward tilt.
Yellow car is still near the jaws at the basket front. Continue a small, slow forward placement motion with closed grip to bring it fully over the left basket.
Both cars now appear inside left basket, with watches in blue and toys in red. Open left jaws and withdraw above the rim to begin reset; correct small right-home drift.
All objects remain in their category baskets. Retract empty left arm within its workspace and gradually restore original orientation, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue left-arm reset toward original position and wrist orientation with open gripper; preserve configuration continuity and leave the sorted baskets undisturbed.
Finish smooth return of left arm to the original EE pose and correct tiny right-home drift, keeping both grippers open. Objects remain in assigned baskets.
